newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firmer on foreign re-entry.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firmer on foreign re-entry.

text.p: The peso recouped lost ground for the second day in a row on Friday, as foreign investors returned to Mexico and local investors sold long dollar positions, traders said.
"Foreigners have been coming back since Thursday afternoon, and that prompted local dealers to sell long (dollar) positions they had bought," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart closed 2.7 and 1 centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.9450/7.9530 and 7.9400/7.9500 per dollar.
The same-day peso had previously closed seven centavos firmer at 7.9400/7.9500 per dollar.
Traders pointed to gains in the stock market and easing pressure on secondary Cetes rates as signs of dollars returning to the Mexican financial markets.

The bourse's leading IPC index was up 48.76 points, or 1.52 percent, at 3,262.09 when the foreign exchange market closed in Mexico. Overnight rates on Cetes were meanwhile down 100 basis points at 30.25 percent.

"Although trading was dull, dollars were clearly in supply today," said a trader. The trader added that another reason for dollars flowing into the market was so that dealers could invest in the local money market over the weekend.
"Pre-weekend deals brought dollars into the market, but it could dry up again on Monday, ahead of the (U.S. presidential) elections (on Tuesday, November 5)," he said.
